neighbours.label: the token just before a revenue/sales/income noun in business text ('% of their turnover', 'the annual sales', 'loss of income', 'in sales'): predicting a measure of business takings
fire: The bakery chain reported a sharp fall in annual revenue after the price rise.
Online orders now make up nearly a third of total sales for the retailer.
The insurance policy covers the loss of income during a forced closure.
The brewery generated over four million euros in sales last year.
Small shops spend up to ten percent of their turnover on rent alone.
The board aims to raise gross revenue to fifty million within five years.
The airline saw a big jump in ticket sales over the holiday season.
Advertising still provides most of the newspaper's operating income.
quiet: The bakery chain reported a sharp fall in staff morale after the price rise.
Online orders now make up nearly a third of all deliveries for the courier.
The insurance policy covers the loss of equipment during a forced closure.
The brewery welcomed over four thousand visitors on its open day last year.
Small shops spend up to ten hours of their week on paperwork alone.
The board aims to raise the number of branches to fifty within five years.
The airline saw a big jump in passenger complaints over the holiday season.
Advertising still fills most of the newspaper's front pages on Sundays.

notes: Card: ' of', ' annual', ' in', ' total', ' gross' before turnover/sales/loans/revenue/income. Probes: 0.22-0.37 on revenue contexts but 'of its staff' also 0.22, so the business frame alone may drive it.
